HYPE.thesis: Strong value capture, but first recorded discovery occurred near an all-time high after a large repricing.
HYPE.invalidation: Value capture weakens materially or crowding/supply overwhelms demand.

UNI.thesis: Protocol value-capture thesis is real, but first recorded Hunter discovery followed a very large 30D repricing.
UNI.invalidation: Fee/burn value capture weakens or spot demand fails.

ARB.thesis: Strong repricing and volume require research, but first Hunter discovery was after a sharp multi-day move.
ARB.invalidation: Activity/revenue thesis fails or supply pressure dominates.

NEAR.thesis: Strong market move merits post-move research, but slow non-price confirmation is incomplete.
NEAR.invalidation: Relative strength/spot demand fades without corroborating non-price evidence.
